name: Telegraph cryptic crossword, All New book 4 No 55

book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Something hanging around front of cave — at least it might be

definitions.text: Something hanging around front of cave — at least it might be

indicators.note: the front of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is kept
'might be' hints that the words could become something else once their letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of cave
taken as written, to be mixed with the letter from cave

explanation.surface: Someone peers at a thing dangling by a cave mouth and guesses what, at the very least, it might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and it also supplies the letters: 'at least it' plus the front of cave rearrange to give STALACTITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalactite is a mineral icicle that hangs from a cave roof, so it is just the thing found dangling near a cave entrance.

clue.text: Part of our capital, thus, goes on small house

blocks.note: so means thus, as in 'do it so'
ho. is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A tour of the capital moves on to look at a little cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'goes on' sets the second piece on top of the first, so SO comes first. 'Our capital' is London for this British paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of London's West End, known for theatres, restaurants and nightlife, so a part of the capital.

clue.text: Circus performer's sack grabbed by a lion, say

indicators.note: something grabbed is held tightly in a grip, so it ends up inside the holder

blocks.note: taken as written
a lion is an example of a big cat
to sack a town is to plunder or rob it

explanation.surface: A circus act's bag is snatched by one of the lions in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. 'Sack' looks like a bag, but it is the verb meaning plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs gymnastic feats such as tumbling and trapeze work, a staple act of the circus.

clue.text: Fools joining one group of people making a killing

definitions.note: a noun phrase here: the act of killing someone

blocks.note: two fools, each an ass
the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a people united by country or culture

explanation.surface: Idiots signing up to a gang of profiteers raking in money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a killing' wants to mean earning a fortune; it is taken literally, as a murder.
explanation.definitionFit: Assassination is the murder of a prominent person, literally the making of a killing.

clue.text: Live among giants, very high people

indicators.note: to be among others is to be surrounded by them, so a piece goes inside

blocks.note: the Titans were the giant elder gods of Greek myth
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Living among giants makes you think of extremely tall people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very high' suggests tall or intoxicated; it refers to altitude, since Tibet is a high plateau.
explanation.definitionFit: Tibetans live on the Tibetan plateau, the highest on Earth at around 4,500 metres above sea level.

clue.text: After short time, parrot turned up in holiday area

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: t is the abbreviation for time
a lory is a brightly coloured parrot of Australasia

explanation.surface: A pet parrot appears briefly at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the reversed parrot behind the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine region of Austria and Italy, popular for skiing and walking holidays.

clue.text: Statistical information turned over at short notice

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped end to end, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a notice in a paper is an advertisement, shortened to ad

explanation.surface: Figures that were handed over in a hurry, with little warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At short notice' looks like a set phrase meaning hurriedly; it is two pieces, 'at' plus a shortened advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for analysis, which is what statistical information consists of.

clue.text: One person in 6 changed, becoming intransigent

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it, so a piece goes inside the other
changed means altered, so the combined letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the answer to 6 across
a man is one person

explanation.surface: One member of a group, changed by the figures, refuses to budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means refusing to change one's mind, and intransigent means unwilling to compromise.

clue.text: Hit an alien ordered to exterminate

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A command to shoot the alien and wipe it out, straight from a sci-fi film.
explanation.definitionFit: To annihilate is to destroy completely, as exterminate means to wipe out entirely.

clue.text: Most of royal family accepting king as deity

indicators.note: most of something is all but a bit of it, so the last letter is dropped
to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a royal dynasty is called a house, as in the House of Windsor
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Most of a royal family treating their king as though he were a god.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUSE loses its last letter to leave HOUS, and R goes inside it to make HORUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Horus is the falcon-headed sky god of ancient Egyptian religion, so he is a deity.

clue.text: Stupid person in prison, with support at home

blocks.note: bird is British slang for prison, from rhyming slang bird-lime for time
a bra is a supporting undergarment; 'with' just adds it on
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A dim inmate behind bars, leaning on help from the family at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdbrain is an informal insult for a foolish person, suggesting a brain the size of a bird's.

clue.text: Major report on the Circle Line that suggests how it all started

definitions.text: that suggests how it all started
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the theory itself

blocks.note: major means big
a report is the sound of an explosion or gunshot, a bang
taken as written
the letter O is circle-shaped
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a rail line

explanation.surface: A big news story about London Underground's Circle Line and how it came to be built.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route, but here circle and line are separate pieces. 'On' just joins the halves.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Bang theory is the scientific account of the universe beginning from a single hot, dense point.

clue.text: As president, your source of news is informal network

blocks.note: George Bush, father or son, was US president
the puzzle comes from the Telegraph, the solver's own newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper jokes that a president hears the news by gossip rather than by reading it.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's paper is the Daily Telegraph, a British daily, so 'your source of news' points to its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush telegraph is the grapevine: news passed rapidly by word of mouth, a phrase from the Australian outback.

clue.text: Finished reading a mystery

blocks.note: something finished is closed, as a case or deal
a book is reading matter

explanation.surface: Someone has just finished a whodunnit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A mystery' looks like the detective novel being read; it is the definition, meaning something not understood.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed book is a subject or person one knows nothing about, something that remains a mystery.

clue.text: People whose capital is held by brigands

definitions.text: People whose capital is held by brigands

blocks.clueFragment: People whose capital is held by brigands
blocks.note: surface reading: a nation whose chief city is under the control of bandits
setter's reading: the capital city's name sits inside the letters of the word brigands, at its second to fifth letters

explanation.surface: A lawless country whose capital has fallen to bandits.
explanation.walkthrough: Nobody holds the city by force: RIGA is hidden in bRIGAnds, and Riga is the capital of Latvia.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvians are the people of Latvia, whose capital Riga is the city spelt out inside the word brigands.

clue.text: Ring telephone on vehicle

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another comes after it, so the piece named first is placed second

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
tel. is the standard abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: An instruction to call someone using the phone in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a verb about phoning; it is the noun for a group of conspirators acting together.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring in the sense of a price-fixing or criminal gang is a cartel, a group of firms or dealers colluding.

clue.text: Disparage Don's article in book with odd title

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters come out in an unusual order
one thing in another is enclosed by it, so a piece goes inside the rest

blocks.note: b. is the abbreviation for book
taken as written, to be rearranged
a Don is a Spanish gentleman, and el is the Spanish word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A university lecturer pans a book with a strange name in his article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like an Oxbridge academic; here it is the Spanish title, so his article is the Spanish definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: To belittle is to make someone or something seem unimportant, which is what disparaging does.

clue.text: Islander putting poles around a gigantic bird

indicators.note: placed around means set on either side, so the remaining pieces sit between them

blocks.note: the two poles are south and north, S and N
taken as written
the moa was a huge flightless bird of New Zealand, now extinct

explanation.surface: A Pacific islander fences in a huge bird between two posts.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '17'' at the start is a print error. S and N go round A plus MOA to give SAMOAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Samoan is a native of Samoa, a group of islands in the South Pacific, so an islander.

clue.text: Get wrong message, in a way, as I'm upset by cut

definitions.text: Get wrong message, in a way

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, and in a down entry that turns the letters upside down

blocks.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
to shear is to cut, as with sheep's wool

explanation.surface: Someone misreads a note, upset about a pay cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' admits that misunderstanding a spoken message is only one way of getting it wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishear is to catch spoken words wrongly, so one way of getting a message wrong.

clue.text: Officer material, soldier defending colony

blocks.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen cloth, often used for uniforms
soldier ants are the caste that guards an ant colony

explanation.surface: Cloth for an officer's uniform, and a trooper standing guard over a settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Officer material' reads as a phrase for someone fit to be promoted; the definition is 'Officer' alone, and material is the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned officer in the army or a police officer of that rank.

clue.text: Bail due to be adjusted — that's within scope of hearing

indicators.note: something adjusted is altered and rearranged, so the letters change their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A court official mentions bail is due for review at a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' sounds like a court session; it means the sense of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Audible means able to be heard, so within the range the ear can pick up.

clue.text: Treated differently, being famous

blocks.note: first meaning: told apart, set apart from others
second meaning: eminent, celebrated

explanation.surface: Celebrities complain that fame makes people treat them differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguished is both the past tense of distinguish (to differentiate) and an adjective meaning eminent and respected.

clue.text: Russian author's goes over line

blocks.note: goes as a plural noun means turns or attempts, so two of them, GO and GO
l. is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A Russian writer crosses a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes' looks like a verb; read as a plural noun it is two GOs. In a down clue 'over' places them above L.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was a nineteenth-century Russian writer, author of Dead Souls and The Overcoat.

clue.text: Boss of establishment where breeding is essential

blocks.note: first meaning: a raised knob or ornamental ...
second meaning: a farm where horses are kept for breeding

explanation.surface: The head of a posh institution where good breeding matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' reads as the head of the establishment, and 'breeding' as good manners; both are other senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is both a decorative knob, called a boss, and a farm keeping animals, especially horses, for breeding.

clue.text: When one normally sleeps nearby, in open

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it, so a piece sits inside the outer word

blocks.note: overt means open, not concealed
nigh is an old word for near

explanation.surface: A camper describes sleeping close by, out in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnight means during the night, the time when people are usually asleep.

clue.text: Complete round-the-world trip, otherwise just part

blocks.note: or, as in 'do it or else', means otherwise
a bit is just a part of something

explanation.surface: A traveller debates going all the way round the globe or only doing a section.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit is to circle a planet; a spacecraft orbiting the Earth completes a circuit of the globe.

clue.text: Get annoyed after king goes into church

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
irk means annoy; the setter stretches it to cover getting annoyed

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper when the king turns up at the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts IRK behind K. 'Goes into' looks like a container signal but only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirk is the Scottish word for a church, as in the Kirk, the Church of Scotland.

clue.text: One slumbering deeply, as he might be

indicators.note: 'might be' suggests the words could turn into something else when their letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone sound asleep, as a man might well be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deeply' seems to describe the slumber, but it starts the letters to rearrange; the definition is just 'One slumbering'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepyhead is an affectionate name for a drowsy person, the kind of person who is dozing off.
